#### Indicators

**Part ID:** `indicators` · [Part guide](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/parts/indicators/) · [Existing image reference](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/assets/illustrations/electrical/EL01.png) · [Existing shop destination](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/parts/)

**Site explanation:** When you move the switch, the flasher sends pulses to the front and rear lamp on that side. Each bulb needs a good earth back to the frame. Stalks break in small falls, holders rust, and a broken bulb or earth on one side usually makes the other bulb on that side flash fast or stay on.

**Site buying checks:** Match bulb type and wattage, for example R10W (12 V 10 W) on the K-Light. A different wattage changes the flash rate with a thermal flasher. LED indicators draw much less current; they need an LED-rated flasher or resistors: Fit LED indicators correctly . Look for an approval mark on the lens. Amber light is required in most countries. Match the mounting thread and stalk length.

#### Instruments

**Part ID:** `instruments` · [Part guide](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/parts/instruments/) · [Existing image reference](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/assets/renders/instruments_analogue.webp) · [Existing shop destination](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/parts/)

**Site explanation:** The instruments tell you speed, distance, fuel and faults. Electronic clusters need a steady 12 V supply, an earth and signals from sensors and switches. Water getting in, vibration, a weak battery or a poor plug make them reset, flicker or go dark. Mechanical speedometers fail when the cable or drive gear wears.

**Site buying checks:** Match make, model and year, plug and wiring. Speedometers are calibrated for wheel size and sensor; a wrong one reads wrong. In many countries changing the odometer reading is illegal. Keep a record of the old reading when fitting a new unit. Mechanical clusters: match the cable fitting.

#### Side stand, clutch and neutral switches

**Part ID:** `interlock_switches` · [Part guide](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/parts/interlock_switches/) · [Existing image reference](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/assets/illustrations/wiring/F23.png) · [Existing shop destination](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/parts/)

**Site explanation:** Typical logic: the starter works only in neutral, or in gear with the clutch pulled; and if the side stand is down while a gear is selected, the engine cuts. On the K-Light the starter relay earth runs through the clutch switch, or through the neutral switch via a diode, and the ECU also reads clutch, neutral and side stand signals. The neutral switch also lights the green N lamp. Switches get dirt, water, rust and bent tabs; wires break at the stand pivot.

**Site buying checks:** Match make, model and year, plug and wire colours. Side stand switches can be normally open or normally closed. Neutral switches: match thread, sealing washer and type (single neutral contact or full gear position switch). Clutch switches: match lever type and plug.

#### Regulator rectifier

**Part ID:** `regulator` · [Part guide](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/parts/regulator/) · [Existing image reference](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/assets/illustrations/wiring/F21.png) · [Existing shop destination](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/parts/part/regulator-rectifier/)

**Site explanation:** The stator makes AC (alternating current), which rises with engine speed. The rectifier part turns it into DC (direct current) to charge the battery. The regulator part stops the voltage rising too high by dumping extra power as heat. That is why it has fins and gets hot. Heat, loose plugs and corroded connectors damage it; when it fails it either stops charging or lets the voltage run too high.

**Site buying checks:** Match make, model and year, or the part number: single-phase or three-phase, number of wires and plug. Some newer types (MOSFET) run cooler; only fit one if it is made for your charging system. Cheap units can overcharge. Test charging voltage after fitting.

#### Speed sensor

**Part ID:** `speed_sensor` · [Part guide](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/parts/speed_sensor/) · [Existing image reference](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/assets/renders/instruments_tft.webp) · [Existing shop destination](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/parts/)

**Site explanation:** As the teeth or magnets pass, the sensor sends pulses. The instruments count them to show speed and distance; on some bikes the ECU also uses the signal. Mud, metal dust, a bent ring, a damaged wire or a loose sensor stop the pulses.

**Site buying checks:** Match the part number, plug and mounting. Sensors differ in type (two-wire or three-wire) and in the gap they need. For hub gear drives, match the drive gear and tangs.

#### Starter motor

**Part ID:** `starter` · [Part guide](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/parts/starter/) · [Existing image reference](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/assets/engine/shots/05-generator-electric-start.webp) · [Existing shop destination](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/parts/)

**Site explanation:** When you press the start button, the relay sends battery current to the motor. It spins fast and turns the engine through the gears until the engine fires. Inside, carbon brushes rub on a copper commutator. Brushes wear shorter, the commutator gets dirty, and water or oil gets inside. The motor draws a very high current, so a weak battery or poor cable shows up here first.

**Site buying checks:** Match make, model and year, or the part number: gear teeth, shaft length, mounting flange and terminal. Brush kits must match the brush size and holder. Cheap motors may have weak magnets and draw more current. Compare weight and finish with the old one.

**Linked site repairs:** [Remove and inspect the starter motor Workshop job · 1 to 2 h assessment](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/starter-motor-service/); [Test the starter circuit Home workshop · 30 to 60 min](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/starter-circuit-test/); [Check the starter clutch Workshop job · 2 to 3 h assessment](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/starter-clutch-check/)

#### Starter clutch

**Part ID:** `starter_clutch` · [Part guide](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/parts/starter_clutch/) · [Existing image reference](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/assets/engine/shots/05-generator-electric-start.webp) · [Existing shop destination](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/parts/)

**Site explanation:** When the starter turns, the rollers lock and the starter gear drives the flywheel and crank. Once the engine fires and runs faster than the starter, the rollers release so the engine does not spin the starter. Springs and rollers wear, the gear face pits, and old or wrong oil makes the rollers stick or slip. MAVCC names it as the most common cause of a starter that spins without turning the engine.

**Site buying checks:** Match engine code: number of rollers, bolt pattern and starter gear teeth. Kits may include rollers, springs and caps only, or the full housing. Check what is in the box. Check the gear hub surface on the new part; it must be smooth and hard.

**Linked site repairs:** [Check the starter clutch Workshop job · 2 to 3 h assessment](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/starter-clutch-check/)

#### Starter relay

**Part ID:** `starter_relay` · [Part guide](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/parts/starter_relay/) · [Existing image reference](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/assets/illustrations/wiring/F23.png) · [Existing shop destination](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/parts/)

**Site explanation:** The start button can only carry a small current. Pressing it powers a coil in the relay, which pulls heavy contacts together and lets battery current flow to the starter motor . The coil's earth often goes through the clutch, neutral or side stand switches, so the starter only works when it is safe. The heavy contacts burn and pit with use; then the relay clicks but the motor does not turn.

**Site buying checks:** Match the part number or make and model: plug shape, coil wires and any built-in fuse. Relays with the same case can have a different coil earth arrangement; match the wiring. Check the rubber boots and mounting are included.

#### Stator and flywheel

**Part ID:** `stator` · [Part guide](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/parts/stator/) · [Existing image reference](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/assets/engine/shots/05-generator-electric-start.webp) · [Existing shop destination](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/parts/)

**Site explanation:** As the magnets spin past the coils they make AC electricity. The regulator rectifier turns this into DC to charge the battery and run the lights. The coils get hot in oil; heat and age break down the varnish on the wire, and a coil shorts or goes open. Loose or wet plugs between the stator and regulator burn.

**Site buying checks:** Match the part number, or make, model and engine. Count coils and wires; single-phase and three-phase stators are not swappable. Check whether the pick-up comes with the stator. Rewound stators are common and can be good, but ask about wire grade and a warranty.

#### Tail and brake light

**Part ID:** `tail_light` · [Part guide](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/parts/tail_light/) · [Existing image reference](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/assets/renders/tail_light.webp) · [Existing shop destination](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/parts/)

**Site explanation:** The tail light shows your bike to drivers behind at night. The brake light comes on bright when either brake light switch closes. Filaments break from vibration; bulb holders rust from water; LED units fail when water gets in. A bulb fitted the wrong way round can light the wrong filament.

**Site buying checks:** Match bulb type and wattage. Two-filament bulbs have offset pins so they fit only one way; do not force them. Look for an approval mark on the lamp. A red lens must stay red: do not fit a clear lens with a coloured bulb unless it is approved. Check the lens gasket is included.

#### Wiring harness and connectors

**Part ID:** `wiring` · [Part guide](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/parts/wiring/) · [Existing image reference](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/assets/renders/wiring_harness.webp) · [Existing shop destination](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/parts/)

**Site explanation:** Each circuit takes power from the battery through a fuse and a switch to its load, then back through the frame (the earth). Wire colours tell you which circuit a wire belongs to. Most electrical faults are not in the parts themselves but in a corroded connector, a loose earth or a chafed wire. Trace the circuits in the Wiring Lab .

**Site buying checks:** A harness must match the model, year and options (kick or electric start, carburettor or fuel injection, CDI or ECU). Use wire of at least the same size, and the same fuse rating. Never fit a bigger fuse to stop a fuse blowing.

### Frame, stands and bodywork

#### Body panels and mudguards

**Part ID:** `bodywork` · [Part guide](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/parts/bodywork/) · [Existing image reference](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/assets/illustrations/frame_body/FB02.png) · [Existing shop destination](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/parts/)

**Site explanation:** Panels keep water, mud and stones off the rider, the engine and the electrics. Mudguards stop the tyres throwing water up. Panels also protect wiring and fuel parts. Hooks and tabs break easily if you pull a panel off the wrong way, and then the panel rattles.

**Site buying checks:** Make, model, year and colour code. Panels from a different year may have different mounting points. Buy the grommets, clips and screws as well; old ones are often broken. Cheap copies may not line up with the mounting holes; compare photos with your bike.

**Linked site repairs:** [Find and fix rattles Home workshop · 20 to 60 min](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/rattle-fix/); [Check chassis fasteners Home workshop · 30 to 60 min](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/fastener-check/); [Check chain guides, sliders and guards Home workshop · 15 to 30 min](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/chain-guide-check/); [Check cooling of the motor and controller Home workshop · 20 to 40 min](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/ev-thermal-check/)

#### Centre stand

**Part ID:** `centre_stand` · [Part guide](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/parts/centre_stand/) · [Existing image reference](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/assets/illustrations/frame_body/FB02.png) · [Existing shop destination](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/parts/)

**Site explanation:** It lets you park on a slope or soft ground, carry loads safely, oil the chain, and work on the rear wheel. You stand on the foot tab and pull the bike back. If the pivot is dry or worn, the stand is hard to use and the bike can roll off. Weak springs let the stand hang down and scrape in corners.

**Site buying checks:** Make, model and year. Pivot shaft diameter, leg length and spring hooks must match. Springs and pivot shafts are often sold separately.

#### Footpegs and foot pedals

**Part ID:** `footpegs` · [Part guide](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/parts/footpegs/) · [Existing image reference](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/assets/illustrations/frame_body/FB02.png) · [Existing shop destination](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/parts/)

**Site explanation:** Pegs carry your weight when standing over bumps and give you a firm place to control the bike. Folding pegs swing up if they touch the ground in a fall or a tight corner, then a spring brings them back down. Pivots dry out and seize, springs break, rubbers wear, and brackets bend or crack in falls.

**Site buying checks:** Make, model, year and position (rider left, rider right, pillion). Mounting holes and pivot pin size must match. Rubber covers are often sold separately. Replace the split pin or clip on the pivot pin with a new one.

#### Mirrors

**Part ID:** `mirrors` · [Part guide](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/parts/mirrors/) · [Existing image reference](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/assets/renders/handlebar.webp) · [Existing shop destination](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/parts/part/mirrors/)

**Site explanation:** Mirrors let you see traffic behind you without turning your head. The arm has a ball joint or pivot so you can aim it. Vibration and knocks loosen the base nut or the joint, so the mirror turns while riding. Cracked glass distorts the view.

**Site buying checks:** Thread size and direction: many bikes use 8 mm or 10 mm threads, and some have a left-hand thread on one side. Check the old mirror. Left and right are often different. Road-legal mirrors carry an approval mark (an "E" in a circle with a number in Europe and some other markets). Cheap mirrors may vibrate badly or have poor glass.

#### Seat and seat lock

**Part ID:** `seat` · [Part guide](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/parts/seat/) · [Existing image reference](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/assets/renders/seat_bench.webp) · [Existing shop destination](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/parts/)

**Site explanation:** The seat carries the rider and passenger and protects the parts under it from rain. A worn lock or broken hook lets the seat move, which is dangerous at speed. A torn cover lets water into the foam, so it stays wet and rots the base.

**Site buying checks:** Make, model and year. Hook and bolt positions must match the frame. Locks come with keys; some bikes use one key for ignition, seat and tank. A single lock may need a new key set. Covers: buy for your model so they fit the base.

#### Side stand and spring

**Part ID:** `side_stand` · [Part guide](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/parts/side_stand/) · [Existing image reference](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/assets/illustrations/frame_body/FB02.png) · [Existing shop destination](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/parts/)

**Site explanation:** The springs pull the stand past a centre point so it stays either fully up or fully down. If a spring is weak or missing, the stand can drop while riding and dig into the road in a left turn, which can throw the rider off. A worn pivot lets the bike lean too far and fall over.

**Site buying checks:** Springs: make, model and year; length, wire thickness and hook shape. Some bikes use two springs, one inside the other. Stand: length and foot shape; a longer stand makes the bike stand too upright and fall over the other way. The stand switch is a separate part: Side stand, clutch and neutral switches .

**Linked site repairs:** [Check the side stand Rider job · 10 to 20 min](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/side-stand-check/); [Check the throttle, brake and stand interlocks Home workshop · 15 to 30 min](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/ev-interlock-check/); [Check chassis fasteners Home workshop · 30 to 60 min](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/fastener-check/); [Test the side stand, clutch and neutral switches Home workshop · 20 to 40 min](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/interlock-switch-test/); [Pre-ride check Rider job · 2 min daily; 10 to 15 min weekly](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/pre-ride-check/); [Periodic service schedule Rider job · reading 10 min; services vary (see each job)](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/service-schedule/)

### Engine

#### Cam chain

**Part ID:** `cam_chain` · [Part guide](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/parts/cam_chain/) · [Existing image reference](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/assets/engine/shots/07-valvetrain.webp) · [Existing shop destination](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/parts/)

**Site explanation:** The chain turns the camshaft at half crank speed so the valves open in time with the piston. A tensioner and guides keep it tight. The chain stretches slowly as its pins wear, faster with dirty oil or long oil change intervals. A slack chain slaps on its guides, and if it jumps a tooth the valves can hit the piston.

**Site buying checks:** Match engine code, chain type (roller or silent/inverted tooth) and number of links. Two chains can look alike and differ by one or two links. Endless chains need the crank side of the engine opened; split chains need a riveting tool and a matching link. Good chains come from known chain makers, with stamped side plates and smooth, even links.

**Linked site repairs:** [Check the cam chain and tensioner Workshop job · 30 min check, 3 to 6 h if parts are replaced](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/cam-chain-check/)

#### Cam chain tensioner and guides

**Part ID:** `cam_tensioner` · [Part guide](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/parts/cam_tensioner/) · [Existing image reference](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/assets/engine/shots/07-valvetrain.webp) · [Existing shop destination](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/parts/)

**Site explanation:** As the chain stretches, the tensioner moves out to take up the slack, so the chain stays quiet and the valve timing stays correct. Modern tensioners are automatic, using a spring and a ratchet, or oil pressure. Older ones have a locking bolt that must be released and locked by hand. Guides are plastic or rubber on metal and wear into grooves; pieces can break off into the oil.

**Site buying checks:** Match engine code. Tensioners that look the same can have different plunger length or spring force. Check the type: automatic ratchet, oil-pressure, or manual-lock. Do not fit a manual one where an automatic one was fitted. Buy a new gasket for the tensioner body. Avoid guides with soft, rough plastic.

**Linked site repairs:** [Check the cam chain and tensioner Workshop job · 30 min check, 3 to 6 h if parts are replaced](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/cam-chain-check/)

#### Camshaft

**Part ID:** `camshaft` · [Part guide](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/parts/camshaft/) · [Existing image reference](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/assets/engine/shots/07-valvetrain.webp) · [Existing shop destination](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/parts/)

**Site explanation:** The camshaft turns at half crank speed. Each lobe lifts a valve open at the right moment and lets the spring close it. Some cams carry a small decompressor that eases kickstarting. Lobes and bearings wear when the oil is dirty or low, and a worn lobe opens the valve less, so the engine loses power.

**Site buying checks:** Match the engine code exactly. Cams with the same shape can have different lobe timing. For OHC engines, check the cam sprocket bolt pattern and timing marks. For pushrod engines, check the gear and decompressor. Fast-road or "racing" cams change idle and fuel use and can hurt reliability. Fit the standard profile for a commuter.

#### Crankcase breather

**Part ID:** `crankcase_breather` · [Part guide](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/parts/crankcase_breather/) · [Existing image reference](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/assets/illustrations/powertrain/F11.png) · [Existing shop destination](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/parts/)

**Site explanation:** A little gas always leaks past the rings into the crankcase (blow-by). The breather lets this gas out, so pressure does not push oil past seals and gaskets. Sending it to the airbox means the fumes are burned in the engine. The breather must let gas out but keep oil in; a separator chamber drops the oil mist back into the engine.

**Site buying checks:** Match the hose inside diameter, length and shape. Use oil-resistant hose, not fuel hose of the wrong grade or garden hose. Fit new clips if the old ones are rusty or loose. Some models have a one-way valve in the line; match its direction arrow.

#### Crankshaft and connecting rod

**Part ID:** `crankshaft` · [Part guide](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/parts/crankshaft/) · [Existing image reference](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/assets/engine/shots/01-whole-engine.webp) · [Existing shop destination](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/parts/)

**Site explanation:** The rod turns the up and down push of the piston into rotation of the crank. The webs carry counterweights to cut vibration. The big end (rod to crank) and main bearings need clean oil under pressure. Dirty or low oil, over-revving or lugging wears these bearings and lets the rod knock.

**Site buying checks:** Match engine code, stroke, rod length and the taper and keyway for the flywheel. Cranks for a kickstart and a non-kick engine can differ. Buy main bearings and crankcase oil seals at the same time, with a gasket set. A good crank is true, with no rust, a smooth big end with no play and clean threads. Ask for runout to be checked on V-blocks before fitting.

#### Cylinder (barrel)

**Part ID:** `cylinder` · [Part guide](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/parts/cylinder/) · [Existing image reference](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/assets/renders/cylinder.webp) · [Existing shop destination](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/parts/)

**Site explanation:** The cylinder guides the piston and, with the rings, seals the pressure of the burning mix. Fins carry heat away into the air on air-cooled engines. The inside wall (the bore) slowly wears oval and tapered, most at the top. Dust that passes a bad air filter wears it fast, and overheating can score it.

**Site buying checks:** Match engine code and bore size. Kits sold as "big bore" change the engine and may not be legal or reliable. Cylinder kits often come with piston, rings, pin and gaskets. Check the piston size marked on the crown matches the bore. Look for a clean, cross-hatched bore, no casting holes in the bore and straight fins. A cheap kit with a poor finish can wear out in weeks.

#### Cylinder head

**Part ID:** `cylinder_head` · [Part guide](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/parts/cylinder_head/) · [Existing image reference](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/assets/renders/cylinder.webp) · [Existing shop destination](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/parts/)

**Site explanation:** The head closes the top of the cylinder so the burning mix can push the piston. On a four-stroke the valves in the head open to let mix in and exhaust out, then close tight for compression. The head gets very hot, so it can warp if the engine overheats, and carbon builds up in the combustion chamber over time.

**Site buying checks:** Match the engine code and model. Heads that look the same can differ in valve size, port shape, plug thread and pushrod or cam layout. Check whether the head comes bare or with valves fitted. A "complete" head still needs the clearances set. Genuine heads have clean casting, smooth ports and straight, crack-free fins. Avoid heads with rough porosity holes, crooked plug threads or valve seats that are not round. Always fit a new head gasket .

#### Drain plug and washer

**Part ID:** `drain_plug` · [Part guide](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/parts/drain_plug/) · [Existing image reference](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/assets/illustrations/powertrain/F11.png) · [Existing shop destination](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/parts/)

**Site explanation:** The plug holds oil in; the washer crushes slightly to make the seal. Over-tightening stretches the threads in the soft aluminium crankcase, and a washer that has been crushed once does not seal well again. Some plugs carry a magnet that catches steel particles.

**Site buying checks:** Match thread size and pitch (for example M12 x 1.5), length and head size. A plug that is too long can hit parts inside. Washers: match inside and outside diameter. Use the material the maker used. On a strainer cap, match the O-ring size and the spring.

#### Engine (complete)

**Part ID:** `engine` · [Part guide](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/parts/engine/) · [Existing image reference](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/assets/engine/shots/01-whole-engine.webp) · [Existing shop destination](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/parts/)

**Site explanation:** The engine burns petrol and air above a piston. The pressure pushes the piston down, and the connecting rod turns the crankshaft. A four-stroke fires once every two turns of the crank; a two-stroke fires every turn. An engine needs four things at the right time: fuel, air, a spark and compression. Most engine faults are one of these missing. See every part move in Under the Engine .

**Site buying checks:** A used or exchange engine must match the frame mounts, the gearbox and final drive, the wiring (CDI or ECU, starter) and the exhaust and carburettor or throttle body. Ask for the engine number and check it matches the papers where your country requires it.

#### Engine mounting bolts

**Part ID:** `engine_mounts` · [Part guide](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/parts/engine_mounts/) · [Existing image reference](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/assets/renders/engine_4t.webp) · [Existing shop destination](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/parts/)

**Site explanation:** The mounts hold the engine in line with the frame and, on many bikes, the engine is part of the frame's strength. Loose bolts let the engine move, which shakes the bike, wears the bolt holes and can crack hangers. Rubber bushes stop vibration reaching the rider and wear out with age.

**Site buying checks:** Match diameter, thread pitch, length and strength grade (the number on the bolt head, such as 8.8). Never fit a weaker or shorter bolt. Match the shoulder length on bolts that pass through bushes. Cheap bolts may be soft steel with no grade mark. Buy marked bolts from a known supplier.

#### Engine oil

**Part ID:** `engine_oil` · [Part guide](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/parts/engine_oil/) · [Existing image reference](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/assets/photos/honda-air-cooled.jpg) · [Existing shop destination](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/parts/part/engine-oil/)

**Site explanation:** Oil keeps a thin film between moving metal parts, carries heat away, holds dirt until the next change, stops rust and helps seal the rings. In a motorcycle it must also let the clutch plates grip. Oil breaks down with heat and fills with soot, fuel and metal. Old oil protects badly, and low oil can destroy an engine in minutes.

**Site buying checks:** Viscosity (for example 10W-30): use the grade in your bike's manual for your climate. The K-Light logs do not state a grade. Quality: an API letter (SJ, SL and later) shows engine protection. Clutch: for a bike with a wet clutch, choose JASO MA (MA1 or MA2). JASO MB oil is made for scooters with a dry CVT clutch and can make a wet clutch slip. Car oils marked "energy conserving" contain friction modifiers that can also cause slip (Lubrizol). Fakes are common. Buy sealed bottles from a known shop. Check the cap seal, clear printing, a batch code and a price that is not far below normal.

#### Engine gaskets

**Part ID:** `gaskets` · [Part guide](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/parts/gaskets/) · [Existing image reference](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/assets/photos/engine-closeup.jpg) · [Existing shop destination](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/parts/)

**Site explanation:** A gasket fills the tiny gaps between two faces so oil, compression and air cannot leak. The head gasket also has to hold combustion pressure and heat. Gaskets harden and shrink with heat and age, and are crushed when first tightened, so a used gasket rarely seals a second time.

**Site buying checks:** Match engine code. Gasket sets are sold as top-end (head, base, cover) or full sets. Head and base gaskets come in thicknesses. Fit the same thickness as the old one, or the compression and valve-to-piston gap change. Check bolt holes, oil holes and dowel holes line up with the old gasket before fitting. Poor gaskets are often missing an oil hole.

**Linked site repairs:** [Replace an engine cover gasket Workshop job · 1 to 3 h assessment and repair (estimate, depends on the cover)](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/cover-gasket-replace/); [Trace an oil leak Home workshop · 30 to 60 min plus a short ride](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/oil-leak-trace/); [Inspect and replace clutch plates and springs Workshop job · 1.5 to 3 h (assessment and plate change, engine in frame)](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/clutch-plate-service/); [Test engine compression Home workshop · 30 to 45 min](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/compression-test/); [Find a coolant leak Home workshop · 30 to 60 min](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/cooling-leak-test/); [Assess bottom end and internal engine damage Workshop job · 1 h assessment; strip 4 to 10 h](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/engine-internal-assessment/); [Assess internal gearbox faults Workshop job · 1 h external checks; internal inspection is usually a full day with engine removal](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/gearbox-assessment/); [Do a leak-down test Workshop job · 30 to 60 min](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/leak-down-test/); [Assess the top end (cylinder, piston, valves) Workshop job · 3 to 6 h strip and measure](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/top-end-assessment/); [Check and adjust valve clearance Home workshop · 45 to 90 min (estimate, screw-and-locknut type)](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/valve-clearance/)

#### Oil filter and strainer

**Part ID:** `oil_filter` · [Part guide](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/parts/oil_filter/) · [Existing image reference](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/assets/illustrations/powertrain/F11.png) · [Existing shop destination](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/parts/part/oil-filter/)

**Site explanation:** The strainer stops large bits reaching the oil pump . The centrifugal filter or paper element catches fine dirt and metal before oil reaches the bearings. When a filter is full, oil bypasses it or flow drops, and wear speeds up.

**Site buying checks:** Know which type your bike has before buying. A generic filter is not a substitute for a strainer or centrifugal filter. Strainers: match screen size, spring and the cap O-ring. Cartridges and spin-ons: match the part number, height, diameter, thread and the bypass valve. Fit new O-rings with every filter. Fake filters can look right outside but have thin paper or no bypass valve. Buy from a known maker or dealer and check the print quality and the box seal.

**Linked site repairs:** [Change the engine oil and clean the strainer Home workshop · 40 to 60 min](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/engine-oil-service/); [Replace the drain plug sealing washer Home workshop · 30 to 45 min (estimate, done with an oil change)](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/drain-plug-seal/); [Assess bottom end and internal engine damage Workshop job · 1 h assessment; strip 4 to 10 h](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/engine-internal-assessment/); [Inspect drained oil for clues Home workshop · 10 to 15 min (estimate, during an oil change)](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/oil-inspect/); [Periodic service schedule Rider job · reading 10 min; services vary (see each job)](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/service-schedule/)

**Linked site symptoms:** [Oil turns black very soon after a change OK to ride](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/problems/oil-darkens-quickly/); [Oil pressure or oil level light is on Stop now](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/problems/oil-warning-light/); [Metal particles or flakes in the oil Do not ride](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/problems/metal-in-oil/); [Oil leaking from the drain plug Do not ride](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/problems/oil-leak-drain-plug/)

#### Oil pump

**Part ID:** `oil_pump` · [Part guide](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/parts/oil_pump/) · [Existing image reference](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/assets/illustrations/powertrain/F11.png) · [Existing shop destination](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/parts/)

**Site explanation:** The pump draws oil from the sump through the strainer and pushes it through the filter to the crank big end, then up a passage to the rocker arms or camshaft. Other parts get oil by splash. The rotors are very close fitting. Grit in dirty oil wears them, and a blocked strainer starves the pump.

**Site buying checks:** Match engine code. Pumps for 100 cc and 125 cc engines of one family can differ in rotor width. Check the drive gear teeth and shaft against the old pump. A good pump turns freely by hand with no tight spots and has a clean, flat body face.

**Linked site repairs:** [Change the engine oil and clean the strainer Home workshop · 40 to 60 min](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/engine-oil-service/); [Assess bottom end and internal engine damage Workshop job · 1 h assessment; strip 4 to 10 h](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/engine-internal-assessment/)

**Linked site symptoms:** [Oil pressure or oil level light is on Stop now](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/problems/oil-warning-light/); [Ticking noise from the top of the engine Ride with care](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/problems/tappet-tick/); [Air-cooled engine overheats Stop now](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/problems/overheating-air/); [Deep knocking from the bottom of the engine Stop now](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/problems/deep-knock/); [Engine has seized or locked up Stop now](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/problems/engine-seized/); [Metal particles or flakes in the oil Do not ride](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/problems/metal-in-oil/); [Whining noise from the engine Ride with care](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/problems/whine-from-engine/)

#### Engine oil seals

**Part ID:** `oil_seals` · [Part guide](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/parts/oil_seals/) · [Existing image reference](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/assets/photos/engine-closeup.jpg) · [Existing shop destination](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/parts/)

**Site explanation:** A thin rubber lip, held by a small spring, wipes the turning shaft so oil stays in and dirt stays out. On a two-stroke the crank seals also hold crankcase pressure, which the engine needs to move the mix; a leaking crank seal makes a two-stroke run lean and badly. Lips harden with heat and age, and grit or a rusty or worn shaft cuts them.

**Site buying checks:** Seals are sized inside diameter x outside diameter x width in mm, for example 20 x 32 x 6. Read the size printed on the old seal or measure the shaft and housing. Match lip type (single or double lip) and any direction arrow. Rubber type matters near heat. Buy from a known seal maker; cheap seals can be hard, out of round or lack the spring.

#### Piston

**Part ID:** `piston` · [Part guide](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/parts/piston/) · [Existing image reference](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/assets/engine/shots/07-valvetrain.webp) · [Existing shop destination](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/parts/)

**Site explanation:** When the mix burns, the pressure pushes the piston down and the connecting rod turns the crankshaft. The piston must stay light, move freely and seal with its rings. It is ground slightly oval so it becomes round when hot. Overheating, a lean mixture or lack of oil can melt the crown or seize the skirt on the bore.

**Site buying checks:** Match the engine code and the size: standard or oversize (for example "+0.25"). The size is marked on the crown or the box. Buy as a kit with rings , pin and clips matched to that piston. Check pin diameter and compression height against the old piston. A wrong height changes compression and can hit the valves. Good pistons have clean machining, no casting holes and crisp ring grooves. Very light, rough pistons are a warning sign.

#### Piston rings

**Part ID:** `piston_rings` · [Part guide](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/parts/piston_rings/) · [Existing image reference](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/assets/engine/shots/07-valvetrain.webp) · [Existing shop destination](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/parts/)

**Site explanation:** The top rings seal the pressure above the piston so it pushes on the piston instead of leaking into the crankcase. The oil ring scrapes oil off the cylinder wall so it does not burn. Rings wear thinner with time, dust and dirty oil. Worn rings let gas and oil pass, and their end gap grows.

**Site buying checks:** Match engine code and piston size: standard or the exact oversize. Ring sets are matched to a brand of piston. Rings from a different piston maker may not fit the grooves. Check the set has every ring: top, second and oil ring with its expander. Check marks: "N", "T", "R" or a dot shows the side that faces up.

#### Pushrods and cam followers

**Part ID:** `pushrods` · [Part guide](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/parts/pushrods/) · [Existing image reference](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/assets/engine/shots/07-valvetrain.webp) · [Existing shop destination](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/parts/)

**Site explanation:** When a cam lobe lifts a follower, the follower pushes its pushrod up, the pushrod tilts the rocker, and the rocker opens the valve. Pushrod engines are simple and tough, and their valve gear needs no chain. The follower pads and shafts wear when oil is dirty, and a bent pushrod stops its valve opening properly.

**Site buying checks:** Match engine code; inlet and exhaust pushrods may differ in length. Buy followers with their shafts and O-rings. On the K-Light the followers mount in the base of the cylinder.

#### Rocker arms and adjusters

**Part ID:** `rocker_arms` · [Part guide](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/parts/rocker_arms/) · [Existing image reference](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/assets/engine/shots/07-valvetrain.webp) · [Existing shop destination](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/parts/)

**Site explanation:** The rocker turns the lift of the cam or pushrod into a push on the valve. The adjuster screw sets a small gap (valve clearance) so the valve can close fully when hot. The rocker shaft and bore wear if oil is dirty or slow to arrive, and the screw tip wears where it touches the valve.

**Site buying checks:** Match engine code and inlet or exhaust position; they can differ. Buy shafts and rockers together if both are worn. Check the adjuster screw and locknut thread. Good rockers have a hard, smooth pad and a bore without scoring.

#### Two-stroke oil pump

**Part ID:** `two_stroke_oil_pump` · [Part guide](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/parts/two_stroke_oil_pump/) · [Existing image reference](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/assets/renders/engine_2t.webp) · [Existing shop destination](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/parts/)

**Site explanation:** A two-stroke has no oil sump; it burns a small amount of oil with every charge to lubricate the crank, rod and piston. The pump gives more oil when the throttle is open and less at idle. If the pump stops, the cable comes off, or air gets into the lines, the engine runs dry and can seize in a few kilometres.

**Site buying checks:** Match make, model and engine. Pump output differs between engines. Use the two-stroke oil grade your bike's manual states; never use four-stroke oil in a two-stroke tank. Match oil line inside diameter, and fit the non-return valve the right way.

**Linked site repairs:** [Check the two-stroke oil pump and lines Workshop job · 30 min check; 1 to 2 h with bleeding and setting](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/two-stroke-oil-pump/)

#### Valve springs

**Part ID:** `valve_springs` · [Part guide](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/parts/valve_springs/) · [Existing image reference](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/assets/engine/shots/07-valvetrain.webp) · [Existing shop destination](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/parts/)

**Site explanation:** The cam or rocker pushes the valve open; the spring pulls it shut again and holds it on its seat. Springs lose length and force after many heat cycles, or after over-revving. A weak spring lets the valve bounce at high revs, which feels like a misfire, and in the worst case the valve can touch the piston.

**Site buying checks:** Match engine code and inner or outer position. Inner and outer springs are different. Compare free length and wire thickness with the old spring. Stiffer "racing" springs wear the cam faster. Buy new collets and retainers if they show wear marks.

**Linked site repairs:** [Assess the top end (cylinder, piston, valves) Workshop job · 3 to 6 h strip and measure](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/top-end-assessment/)

#### Valves

**Part ID:** `valves` · [Part guide](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/parts/valves/) · [Existing image reference](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/assets/engine/shots/07-valvetrain.webp) · [Existing shop destination](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/parts/)

**Site explanation:** The inlet valve opens to let fuel and air in; the exhaust valve opens to let burnt gas out. Both close tight for compression. A small gap (valve clearance) lets the valve close fully when hot. If that gap closes up, the valve cannot seat and its edge burns. A rubber stem seal stops oil running down the guide.

**Site buying checks:** Match engine code and position: inlet and exhaust valves are different sizes and materials. Never swap them. Check head diameter, stem diameter and overall length against the old valve. Buy new stem seals and, if the guide is worn, new guides. Good valves have a smooth, even face and straight stem.

### Ignition

#### CDI unit

**Part ID:** `cdi` · [Part guide](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/parts/cdi/) · [Existing image reference](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/assets/engine/shots/05-generator-electric-start.webp) · [Existing shop destination](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/parts/)

**Site explanation:** The CDI charges a capacitor to a few hundred volts. When the pick-up pulse arrives, it dumps that charge into the ignition coil , which makes the spark. It also sets the timing and moves it earlier as revs rise, and on many bikes sets a rev limit. CDIs fail from heat, water and vibration, but they are a less common cause of no spark than plugs, caps, wiring and switches.

**Site buying checks:** Match the part number on the label, and AC or DC type. Plugs that fit are not proof of a match: the timing curve and rev limit differ. "Racing" or unlimited CDIs change timing and can cause pinking and engine damage. Cheap copies are common. Buy from a dealer or a known ignition maker, and keep the receipt in case it fails early.

#### ECU

**Part ID:** `ecu` · [Part guide](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/parts/ecu/) · [Existing image reference](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/assets/illustrations/powertrain/F12.png) · [Existing shop destination](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/parts/)

**Site explanation:** The ECU reads the crank sensor , throttle, pressure and temperature sensors and the oxygen sensor . It then sets injector opening time, spark timing and idle air. It runs the fuel pump and lights the engine warning light when it sees a fault, storing a code. True ECU failure is rare; most faults are in sensors, wiring, plugs and earths. Voltage spikes, jump starts from a car, reverse polarity and water can damage it.

**Site buying checks:** Match the part number and software version on the label. ECUs that fit the same plug can have different fuel maps. Used ECUs from another bike may not work if the bike has an immobiliser. Avoid "remapped" or tuning ECUs on a commuter; they can raise fuel use and engine heat.

#### Ignition coil and plug cap

**Part ID:** `ignition_coil` · [Part guide](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/parts/ignition_coil/) · [Existing image reference](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/assets/engine/shots/05-generator-electric-start.webp) · [Existing shop destination](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/parts/)

**Site explanation:** The coil is a transformer. A low voltage pulse in its primary winding becomes many thousands of volts in the secondary winding, enough to jump the plug gap under compression. Heat and vibration crack the windings inside, so a coil can work cold and fail hot. Water and dirt let the spark track down the outside of the lead or cap instead of reaching the plug.

**Site buying checks:** Match make, model and year, or the coil part number. CDI and transistor (ECU) ignitions use different coils. Match the plug cap: straight or angled, with or without resistor, and the right fit on the plug top. Cheap coils may give a weak spark or fail when hot. Buy from a dealer or known ignition maker.

#### Ignition pick-up

**Part ID:** `pickup` · [Part guide](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/parts/pickup/) · [Existing image reference](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/assets/engine/shots/05-generator-electric-start.webp) · [Existing shop destination](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/parts/)

**Site explanation:** Each time the bump passes, the pick-up makes a small voltage pulse. The CDI or ECU uses this pulse to know where the piston is and when to fire the spark (and, on injection, when to inject). Without a pulse there is no spark at all. Heat, oil, a damaged wire or metal dirt on the magnet can weaken the signal; a large gap to the flywheel makes it too weak at cranking speed.

**Site buying checks:** Match the part number or make and model. On many bikes the pick-up is sold only with the stator plate. Match the plug, wire length and mounting holes. Air gap to the flywheel matters; keep any shims.

#### Spark plug

**Part ID:** `spark_plug` · [Part guide](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/parts/spark_plug/) · [Existing image reference](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/assets/renders/photo/render-plug.jpg) · [Existing shop destination](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/parts/part/spark-plug/)

**Site explanation:** The coil sends a very high voltage down to the plug, and a spark jumps the gap and lights the fuel and air mix. The plug must stay hot enough to burn off soot but cool enough not to glow. How hot it runs is its heat range. Electrodes wear round and the gap grows, so the spark gets weaker. The colour of the tip tells you how the engine is running.

**Site buying checks:** Thread diameter and reach (length of thread), heat range , resistor type and tip type must all match. Each maker codes these differently. On NGK and Denso a higher number is a colder plug; on Champion a higher number is hotter. The K-Light plug is D7RTC . Use the plug maker's own cross-reference chart to find an equivalent; do not guess from the letters. A projected tip in an engine that does not call for one can hit the piston. Fakes: NGK lists smudged printing, machining marks on the crimp and shell, a missing lot number on the hex, and a centre electrode that looks wrong. Buy from a trusted dealer.

### Transmission

#### Drive chain

**Part ID:** `chain` · [Part guide](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/parts/chain/) · [Existing image reference](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/assets/renders/photo/render-chain.jpg) · [Existing shop destination](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/parts/part/chain-sprocket-kit/)

**Site explanation:** It carries the engine's power to the rear wheel. Each link has rollers that sit between the sprocket teeth. The chain needs a little slack, because the rear wheel moves up and down on the swingarm. Too slack and it slaps and can jump off; too tight and it pulls on the gearbox and wheel bearings and makes the wheel drag.

**Site buying checks:** Size : the pitch and width, written on the side plates (for example 428 on many 100 to 150 cc bikes). Number of links : count them or check your manual. Type : plain, or O-ring for longer life. O-ring chains need a lubricant that is safe for the rings. Joining link : a clip link or a rivet link. Fit the clip with its closed end facing the direction the chain moves.

**Linked site repairs:** [Check and adjust chain slack Rider job · 20 to 30 min](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/chain-adjust/); [Clean and lubricate the chain Rider job · 15 to 30 min](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/chain-clean-lube/); [Check the chain for wear Home workshop · 15 to 20 min](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/chain-wear-check/); [Replace the chain and sprockets Workshop job · 1 to 2.5 h](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/chain-sprocket-replace/); [Check for brake drag Home workshop · 15 to 30 min](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/brake-drag-check/); [Check chain guides, sliders and guards Home workshop · 15 to 30 min](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/chain-guide-check/); [Pre-delivery inspection Workshop job · about 1.5 to 3 h including assembly and test ride](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/pre-delivery-inspection/); [Pre-ride check Rider job · 2 min daily; 10 to 15 min weekly](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/pre-ride-check/); [Bring a bike back into use after storage Home workshop · 2 to 4 h](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/recommission-after-storage/); [Periodic service schedule Rider job · reading 10 min; services vary (see each job)](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/service-schedule/); [Inspect sprockets Rider job · 10 to 20 min](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/sprocket-inspect/); [Replace the output shaft seal Workshop job · 1 to 2 h (estimate, chain bikes)](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/sprocket-shaft-seal/); [Check the swingarm pivot Home workshop · 20 to 45 min](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/swingarm-check/); [Remove and refit the rear wheel Home workshop · 30 to 60 min](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/wheel-remove-rear/)

#### Chain guide and slider

**Part ID:** `chain_guide` · [Part guide](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/parts/chain_guide/) · [Existing image reference](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/assets/illustrations/transmission/F15.png) · [Existing shop destination](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/parts/)

**Site explanation:** When the suspension moves, the chain touches the swingarm. The slider is a cheap wear part that takes this rubbing instead of the swingarm. The guide keeps the chain lined up with the rear sprocket, and the guard keeps clothes, fingers and dirt away. A loose chain wears through the slider fast.

**Site buying checks:** Make, model and year; check the swingarm shape and fixing points. Sliders are usually model-specific. Universal ones rarely fit well. Guards and chain cases must clear the chain at full suspension travel.

**Linked site repairs:** [Check the swingarm pivot Home workshop · 20 to 45 min](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/swingarm-check/); [Check and adjust chain slack Rider job · 20 to 30 min](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/chain-adjust/); [Check chain guides, sliders and guards Home workshop · 15 to 30 min](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/chain-guide-check/); [Replace the chain and sprockets Workshop job · 1 to 2.5 h](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/chain-sprocket-replace/); [Find and fix rattles Home workshop · 20 to 60 min](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/rattle-fix/)

**Linked site symptoms:** [Chain rubs on the guard, slider or swingarm Ride with care](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/problems/chain-rubbing/); [Chain is noisy, clattering or slapping Ride with care](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/problems/chain-noise/); [Chain jumps teeth or comes off the sprockets Stop now](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/problems/chain-jumps/); [Rattling from panels, mudguards or the seat OK to ride](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/problems/bodywork-rattle/); [Chain has snapped Stop now](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/problems/chain-snapped/); [Chain needs adjusting very often Ride with care](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/problems/chain-stretches-fast/)

#### Clutch assembly

**Part ID:** `clutch` · [Part guide](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/parts/clutch/) · [Existing image reference](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/assets/engine/shots/03-clutch-cutaway-pulled.webp) · [Existing shop destination](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/parts/)

**Site explanation:** Friction plates and steel plates alternate. Springs squeeze them together so the engine drives the gearbox. When you pull the lever, a cable or hydraulic line lifts the pressure plate, the plates separate, and the engine turns without driving the wheel. This lets you pull away, change gear and stop without stalling. See it working in Under the Engine .

**Site buying checks:** Buy a kit for your exact model: number of plates, size and tabs must match. Use engine oil rated for wet clutches (JASO MA or MA2 for most motorcycles). Car oils with friction modifiers can make the clutch slip.

**Linked site repairs:** [Adjust clutch lever free play Rider job · 10 to 15 min](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/clutch-cable-adjust/); [Inspect and replace clutch plates and springs Workshop job · 1.5 to 3 h (assessment and plate change, engine in frame)](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/clutch-plate-service/); [Check a semi-automatic or centrifugal clutch Workshop job · 30 min (outside checks); 1.5 to 3 h workshop assessment](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/auto-clutch-check/); [Bleed a hydraulic clutch Home workshop · 30 to 45 min](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/clutch-bleed/); [Assess internal gearbox faults Workshop job · 1 h external checks; internal inspection is usually a full day with engine removal](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/gearbox-assessment/); [Check the kickstart mechanism Workshop job · 15 min outside checks; 2 to 4 h internal assessment](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/kickstart-check/); [Road test to diagnose a fault Rider job · 15 to 30 min](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/road-test/)

#### Clutch cable

**Part ID:** `clutch_cable` · [Part guide](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/parts/clutch_cable/) · [Existing image reference](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/assets/engine/shots/03-clutch-cutaway-pulled.webp) · [Existing shop destination](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/parts/part/clutch-cable/)

**Site explanation:** When you pull the lever, the inner wire moves and turns the release arm, which takes spring pressure off the clutch plates. A small amount of slack at the lever (free play) makes sure the clutch is fully clamped when the lever is released. Cables stretch, rust, fray at the ends and get stiff when dry or badly routed.

**Site buying checks:** Make, model and year. Length, end fittings (barrel or ball nipple), adjuster type and outer length must match. Compare the new cable with the old one side by side before fitting. Some cables are lined with plastic and should not be oiled with thick oil; follow the maker's note. Cheap cables often have thin inner wire and soft outer sleeves that compress, giving a spongy lever.

**Linked site repairs:** [Replace the clutch cable Home workshop · 30 to 60 min](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/clutch-cable-replace/); [Adjust clutch lever free play Rider job · 10 to 15 min](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/clutch-cable-adjust/); [Lubricate control cables Rider job · 20 to 40 min](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/cable-lube/); [Inspect and replace clutch plates and springs Workshop job · 1.5 to 3 h (assessment and plate change, engine in frame)](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/clutch-plate-service/); [Service brake and clutch lever pivots Rider job · 15 to 30 min](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/lever-service/); [Pre-delivery inspection Workshop job · about 1.5 to 3 h including assembly and test ride](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/pre-delivery-inspection/); [Periodic service schedule Rider job · reading 10 min; services vary (see each job)](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/service-schedule/)

#### Clutch plates and springs

**Part ID:** `clutch_plates` · [Part guide](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/parts/clutch_plates/) · [Existing image reference](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/assets/engine/shots/03-clutch-cutaway-pulled.webp) · [Existing shop destination](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/parts/part/clutch-plates/)

**Site explanation:** Spring force clamps friction plates against steel plates so they turn together. Each time you slip the clutch to pull away, some lining wears off and heat builds up. Over time the linings get thinner, springs get shorter and weaker, and steel plates can warp from heat. Thin plates or weak springs cannot hold full power. Warped plates do not separate cleanly.

**Site buying checks:** Make, model, year and engine code. Plate count, thickness, outer diameter and tab shape must all match the old ones. Lay a new plate on an old one to compare. Some engines use plates of different thickness or a special first or last plate: keep the old ones in order. Genuine (OEM) kits are reliable. Good aftermarket kits name the bike model on the box. Avoid unbranded kits with uneven lining, loose lining edges or rough tabs. Soak new friction plates in the engine oil before fitting.

**Linked site repairs:** [Inspect and replace clutch plates and springs Workshop job · 1.5 to 3 h (assessment and plate change, engine in frame)](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/clutch-plate-service/); [Adjust clutch lever free play Rider job · 10 to 15 min](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/clutch-cable-adjust/); [Check a semi-automatic or centrifugal clutch Workshop job · 30 min (outside checks); 1.5 to 3 h workshop assessment](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/auto-clutch-check/); [Check the kickstart mechanism Workshop job · 15 min outside checks; 2 to 4 h internal assessment](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/kickstart-check/)

#### Cush drive rubbers

**Part ID:** `cush_drive` · [Part guide](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/parts/cush_drive/) · [Existing image reference](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/assets/renders/rear_sprocket.webp) · [Existing shop destination](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/parts/)

**Site explanation:** The rubbers soften the shock each time you open or close the throttle or change gear. This protects the chain, sprockets and gearbox and makes the ride smoother. Over time the rubber hardens, cracks and shrinks, leaving a gap. Then the carrier knocks against the hub with every throttle change.

**Site buying checks:** Make, model and year, front or rear wheel type (cast or spoked). Shape and number of blocks must match the hub pockets. Count them before ordering. Some bikes use one moulded rubber ring; others use separate blocks. Cheap rubbers can be too soft or the wrong size. A good set fits snugly and needs a little push to seat.

**Linked site repairs:** [Remove and refit the rear wheel Home workshop · 30 to 60 min](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/wheel-remove-rear/); [Check the cush drive rubbers Home workshop · 30 to 60 min](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/cush-drive-check/); [Replace the chain and sprockets Workshop job · 1 to 2.5 h](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/chain-sprocket-replace/); [Inspect sprockets Rider job · 10 to 20 min](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/sprocket-inspect/); [Replace wheel bearings Workshop job · assessment 20 min; replacement about 45 to 90 min per wheel](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/wheel-bearing-replace/)

#### Scooter drive belt

**Part ID:** `cvt_belt` · [Part guide](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/parts/cvt_belt/) · [Existing image reference](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/assets/photos/scooter-cvt-workshop.jpg) · [Existing shop destination](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/parts/part/drive-belt/)

**Site explanation:** Each pulley is two cone-shaped halves. When the front halves close together, the belt rides high on a large radius; at the back the halves open and the belt sits low. This changes the gear ratio smoothly as speed rises. The belt carries all the power by gripping the pulley faces, so it wears thinner, cracks and gets hard with heat. A narrow belt sits lower in the pulleys, so top speed falls.

**Site buying checks:** The belt code printed on the old belt: it gives length and width. Match it exactly. Make, model, year and engine size. Belts for 110, 125 and 150 cc versions of one scooter often differ. Buy a belt in a sealed sleeve with the maker's name and part number. Very cheap belts may be the wrong rubber and break early.

#### Scooter clutch and bell

**Part ID:** `cvt_clutch` · [Part guide](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/parts/cvt_clutch/) · [Existing image reference](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/assets/photos/scooter-cvt-workshop.jpg) · [Existing shop destination](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/parts/part/cvt-clutch-shoes/)

**Site explanation:** At idle the springs hold the shoes inward, so the wheel does not turn. As engine speed rises, the shoes are thrown outward and grip the inside of the bell, driving the wheel. The linings wear thinner and can glaze. The bell can wear a groove or go out of round. Weak springs let the clutch grip too early.

**Site buying checks:** Make, model, year and engine size. Bell inside diameter and shoe size must match. Buy shoes, springs and bell together if the bell is worn. Clutch spring strength sets when the clutch bites; use standard springs unless you know why you are changing. Avoid shoes with loose or thin lining, or no maker marking.

#### Variator rollers and sliders

**Part ID:** `cvt_rollers` · [Part guide](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/parts/cvt_rollers/) · [Existing image reference](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/assets/illustrations/transmission/F16.png) · [Existing shop destination](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/parts/part/roller-weights/)

**Site explanation:** As engine speed rises, the rollers are thrown outward along ramps. This pushes the moving half of the front pulley toward the fixed half, so the belt climbs to a larger radius and the gearing gets taller. Roller weight decides at what engine speed the scooter changes up. Worn rollers develop flat spots, stop rolling and slide instead, which makes the ratio change in jumps.

**Site buying checks:** Size : diameter and width in mm, for example a code like 16×13. Measure the old roller. Weight : in grams, usually printed on the side. Use the standard weight from the manual. Lighter rollers make the engine rev higher; heavier rollers make it labour. Make, model and engine size. Sliders and ramp plates are model-specific. Avoid rollers with seams, rough surfaces or mixed weights in one pack.

**Linked site repairs:** [Check variator rollers and sliders Home workshop · 45 to 90 min](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/cvt-roller-check/); [Inspect and replace the scooter drive belt Home workshop · 45 to 90 min](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/cvt-belt-replace/)

#### Front sprocket

**Part ID:** `front_sprocket` · [Part guide](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/parts/front_sprocket/) · [Existing image reference](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/assets/engine/shots/01-whole-engine.webp) · [Existing shop destination](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/parts/part/chain-sprocket-kit/)

**Site explanation:** The gearbox turns the front sprocket, which pulls the chain. Because it is small, each tooth does more work than a tooth on the rear sprocket, so it often wears faster. The number of teeth sets the gearing: one tooth fewer gives stronger pulling but lower top speed and more fuel use.

**Site buying checks:** Chain size (for example 428), tooth count and spline pattern of the output shaft. Offset (how far the teeth sit from the mounting face) must match, or the chain runs out of line. Match make, model, year and engine code; the tooth count is usually stamped on the face. Changing the tooth count changes the speedometer reading on bikes that measure speed at the gearbox. Good sprockets have hardened, evenly cut teeth. Soft cheap sprockets wear in weeks.

**Linked site repairs:** [Inspect sprockets Rider job · 10 to 20 min](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/sprocket-inspect/); [Replace the chain and sprockets Workshop job · 1 to 2.5 h](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/chain-sprocket-replace/); [Clean and lubricate the chain Rider job · 15 to 30 min](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/chain-clean-lube/); [Check the chain for wear Home workshop · 15 to 20 min](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/chain-wear-check/); [Replace the output shaft seal Workshop job · 1 to 2 h (estimate, chain bikes)](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/sprocket-shaft-seal/)

#### Gear lever

**Part ID:** `gear_lever` · [Part guide](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/parts/gear_lever/) · [Existing image reference](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/assets/engine/shots/04-shift-drum-star-detent.webp) · [Existing shop destination](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/parts/)

**Site explanation:** Pressing down or lifting the lever turns the shift spindle, which changes gear inside the engine. The lever is held on by a pinch bolt through a slot. Splines on the spindle and in the lever stop it from slipping. Drops and kerbs bend levers; a loose pinch bolt lets the splines wear smooth.

**Site buying checks:** Make, model and year. Spline count and the inner diameter of the clamp must match the spindle. Lever length and angle change your foot position: compare with the old lever. Linkage type levers also need the correct rod and ball joints. Replace the pinch bolt if its thread is damaged.

**Linked site repairs:** [Refit or replace the gear lever Home workshop · 15 to 30 min](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/gear-lever-replace/); [Check the gear lever and shift linkage Home workshop · 15 to 30 min](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/gearshift-check/); [Check a semi-automatic or centrifugal clutch Workshop job · 30 min (outside checks); 1.5 to 3 h workshop assessment](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/auto-clutch-check/); [Service footpegs and foot pedals Home workshop · 20 to 45 min](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/pedal-peg-service/)

**Linked site symptoms:** [Gear lever is loose, bent or slipping on its shaft Ride with care](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/problems/gear-lever-loose/); [Gear lever does not spring back Ride with care](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/problems/gear-lever-no-return/); [Gears are hard to select Ride with care](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/problems/hard-gear-change/); [Semi-automatic clutch (step-through) slips or engages roughly Ride with care](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/problems/auto-clutch-fault/); [Finds false neutrals between gears Ride with care](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/problems/false-neutral/); [Hard to find neutral OK to ride](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/problems/hard-to-find-neutral/); [Jumps out of gear under load Ride with care](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/problems/jumps-out-of-gear/); [Oil leaking from an engine side cover Ride with care](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/problems/oil-leak-cover/); [Oil leaking behind the front sprocket Ride with care](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/problems/oil-leak-sprocket/); [Foot pedal or footpeg is stiff, bent or loose Ride with care](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/problems/pedal-stiff/); [Stuck in one gear Do not ride](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/problems/stuck-in-gear/)

#### Final drive gear oil

**Part ID:** `gear_oil` · [Part guide](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/parts/gear_oil/) · [Existing image reference](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/assets/illustrations/transmission/F16.png) · [Existing shop destination](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/parts/part/gear-oil/)

**Site explanation:** The oil coats the gears and bearings so metal does not touch metal. Gear oil is thicker than engine oil and made for high tooth pressure. It is a small amount, so it gets dirty quickly if it is never changed. If the case seal leaks, the level drops and oil can reach the rear brake or tyre.

**Site buying checks:** Viscosity and type written in the manual or on the case, for example a gear oil grade or, on some scooters, engine oil. Do not guess. Quantity is small and exact; buy the amount the manual gives and measure it. Buy sealed bottles from a known brand. Refilled or unlabelled bottles may be old engine oil. New sealing washers for the drain and filler bolts.

**Linked site repairs:** [Change scooter final drive oil Home workshop · 20 to 40 min](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/scooter-gear-oil/); [Check the scooter clutch and bell Workshop job · 20 min (look inside the case); 1 to 2 h workshop assessment](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/cvt-clutch-check/)

**Linked site symptoms:** [Oil leaking from the scooter rear gear case Ride with care](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/problems/cvt-gear-oil-leak/); [Noise from the scooter drive case Ride with care](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/problems/cvt-noise/); [Scooter drive belt has broken Stop now](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/problems/cvt-belt-broken/); [Scooter revs but accelerates slowly Ride with care](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/problems/cvt-slip/)

#### Gearbox

**Part ID:** `gearbox` · [Part guide](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/parts/gearbox/) · [Existing image reference](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/assets/engine/shots/02-gearbox-function-colours.webp) · [Existing shop destination](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/parts/)

**Site explanation:** Two shafts carry pairs of gears that are always in mesh. The gear pedal turns a shift drum, which moves forks that slide gears sideways until their dogs lock one pair to its shaft. Only that pair carries the power. Low gears give force for pulling away and climbing; high gears give speed. Most commuter bikes shift 1-N-2-3-4-5. See the drum, forks and dogs move in Under the Engine , and gear ratios explained in the crash course .

**Site buying checks:** Gears and forks must match the model and year exactly. Replace worn dogs in matching pairs. Use the engine oil grade in your manual; the gearbox shares it.

**Linked site repairs:** [Assess internal gearbox faults Workshop job · 1 h external checks; internal inspection is usually a full day with engine removal](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/gearbox-assessment/); [Check the gear lever and shift linkage Home workshop · 15 to 30 min](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/gearshift-check/); [Check the kickstart mechanism Workshop job · 15 min outside checks; 2 to 4 h internal assessment](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/kickstart-check/)

**Linked site symptoms:** [Gears are hard to select Ride with care](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/problems/hard-gear-change/); [Jumps out of gear under load Ride with care](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/problems/jumps-out-of-gear/); [Finds false neutrals between gears Ride with care](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/problems/false-neutral/); [Whining noise in one or more gears Ride with care](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/problems/gearbox-whine/); [Metal particles or flakes in the oil Do not ride](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/problems/metal-in-oil/); [Rumbling or growling from inside the engine Do not ride](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/problems/bearing-rumble/); [Engine dies when the side stand moves or the bike is put in gear Ride with care](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/problems/dies-side-stand/); [Gear lever does not spring back Ride with care](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/problems/gear-lever-no-return/); [Kickstarter will not move or does not spring back Ride with care](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/problems/kickstart-jammed/); [Stuck in one gear Do not ride](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/problems/stuck-in-gear/); [Whining noise from the engine Ride with care](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/problems/whine-from-engine/)
