#### Kickstarter

**Part ID:** `kickstarter` · [Part guide](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/parts/kickstarter/) · [Existing image reference](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/assets/engine/shots/06-kickstart.webp) · [Existing shop destination](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/parts/)

**Site explanation:** When you push the lever down, the ratchet locks onto a gear and turns the engine. When the engine fires, the ratchet slips so the lever is not driven. The return spring brings the lever back to the top. Worn ratchet teeth make the lever slip. A broken return spring leaves the lever hanging.

**Site buying checks:** What people usually buy: the lever, its pinch bolt and the return spring. Match make, model, year and engine code. Spline count and lever length must match. Some engines use a different kick shaft for electric-start versions.

**Linked site repairs:** [Check the kickstart mechanism Workshop job · 15 min outside checks; 2 to 4 h internal assessment](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/kickstart-check/); [Service footpegs and foot pedals Home workshop · 20 to 45 min](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/pedal-peg-service/)

**Linked site symptoms:** [Kickstarter slips or turns without turning the engine Ride with care](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/problems/kickstart-slips/); [Kickstarter will not move or does not spring back Ride with care](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/problems/kickstart-jammed/); [Kickstarter kicks back against my foot Ride with care](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/problems/kickstart-kickback/); [Engine has seized or locked up Stop now](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/problems/engine-seized/); [Oil leaking from an engine side cover Ride with care](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/problems/oil-leak-cover/); [Foot pedal or footpeg is stiff, bent or loose Ride with care](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/problems/pedal-stiff/)

**Proposed model links (0):** No model-level assignment yet. Resolve specific hardware before adding this component; absence here does not mean incompatible.

#### Rear sprocket

**Part ID:** `rear_sprocket` · [Part guide](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/parts/rear_sprocket/) · [Existing image reference](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/assets/renders/rear_sprocket.webp) · [Existing shop destination](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/parts/part/chain-sprocket-kit/)

**Site explanation:** The chain pulls the rear sprocket round, and the sprocket turns the wheel. The ratio between front and rear tooth counts sets the gearing. As the chain stretches it rides higher on the teeth and wears them into a hooked shape, which then wears a new chain quickly.

**Site buying checks:** Chain size (for example 428) and tooth count, stamped on the face. Bolt circle, number of bolt holes and centre bore must match the hub or carrier. Thickness matters: a sprocket for a different chain width will not fit. Steel sprockets last longer than alloy ones on commuter bikes. Check the box names your bike model. Avoid sprockets with rough, uneven teeth or no markings.

**Linked site repairs:** [Inspect sprockets Rider job · 10 to 20 min](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/sprocket-inspect/); [Replace the chain and sprockets Workshop job · 1 to 2.5 h](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/chain-sprocket-replace/); [Check and adjust chain slack Rider job · 20 to 30 min](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/chain-adjust/); [Clean and lubricate the chain Rider job · 15 to 30 min](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/chain-clean-lube/); [Check the chain for wear Home workshop · 15 to 20 min](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/chain-wear-check/); [Check the cush drive rubbers Home workshop · 30 to 60 min](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/cush-drive-check/); [Check chassis fasteners Home workshop · 30 to 60 min](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/fastener-check/); [Remove and refit the rear wheel Home workshop · 30 to 60 min](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/wheel-remove-rear/)

**Linked site symptoms:** [Sprocket teeth are hooked, sharp or broken Ride with care](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/problems/sprocket-worn/); [Chain jumps teeth or comes off the sprockets Stop now](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/problems/chain-jumps/); [Chain is noisy, clattering or slapping Ride with care](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/problems/chain-noise/); [Chain is tight in some places and slack in others Ride with care](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/problems/chain-tight-spots/); [Chain is dry, rusty or has stiff links Ride with care](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/problems/chain-dry-rusty/); [Chain rubs on the guard, slider or swingarm Ride with care](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/problems/chain-rubbing/); [Chain has snapped Stop now](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/problems/chain-snapped/); [Chain needs adjusting very often Ride with care](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/problems/chain-stretches-fast/); [Clunk or snatch from the rear wheel when opening and closing the throttle Ride with care](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/problems/cush-drive-clunk/); [Bike judders or jerks when pulling away Ride with care](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/problems/ev-judder/); [Grinding, clicking or growling from the motor Ride with care](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/problems/ev-motor-noise/); [Struggles to climb hills or carry a passenger Ride with care](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/problems/poor-hill-climbing/); [Vibration at certain speeds Ride with care](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/problems/speed-vibration/); [Surges or jerks at steady cruising speed Ride with care](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/problems/surging-cruise/)

#### Gear shift mechanism

**Part ID:** `shift_mechanism` · [Part guide](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/parts/shift_mechanism/) · [Existing image reference](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/assets/engine/shots/04-shift-drum-star-detent.webp) · [Existing shop destination](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/parts/)

**Site explanation:** Each press of the lever turns the spindle, which turns the drum by one step. The stopper arm drops into a notch on the star plate to hold the drum in each gear. The return spring brings the lever back so it is ready for the next change. A weak stopper spring lets the drum creep out of gear. A broken return spring leaves the lever hanging down.

**Site buying checks:** Engine code and gearbox type. Spindle spline count and length must match the old one. Springs are model-specific: match wire thickness, coil count and hook shape. Buy a new cover gasket and the spindle oil seal at the same time.

**Linked site repairs:** [Check the gear lever and shift linkage Home workshop · 15 to 30 min](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/gearshift-check/); [Assess internal gearbox faults Workshop job · 1 h external checks; internal inspection is usually a full day with engine removal](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/gearbox-assessment/); [Check a semi-automatic or centrifugal clutch Workshop job · 30 min (outside checks); 1.5 to 3 h workshop assessment](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/auto-clutch-check/); [Refit or replace the gear lever Home workshop · 15 to 30 min](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/gear-lever-replace/)

### Chassis, steering and suspension

#### Choke cable

**Part ID:** `choke_cable` · [Part guide](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/parts/choke_cable/) · [Existing image reference](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/assets/illustrations/controls/F05.png) · [Existing shop destination](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/parts/)

**Site explanation:** Pulling the choke lever pulls the cable, which closes a flap or opens a starter jet in the carburettor. This gives a richer mixture so a cold engine starts. When the lever is pushed back, a spring should close the choke fully. If the cable sticks or is out of adjustment, the choke may never work, or may stay partly on and waste fuel.

**Site buying checks:** Make, model and year; carburettor type. Length, end fittings and the carburettor-end plunger or nipple must match. Compare with the old cable before fitting.

#### Fork oil

**Part ID:** `fork_oil` · [Part guide](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/parts/fork_oil/) · [Existing image reference](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/assets/illustrations/chassis/F18.png) · [Existing shop destination](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/parts/part/fork-seals/)

**Site explanation:** When the fork moves, oil is pushed through small holes. The oil's thickness (viscosity) sets how much it resists: thicker oil gives slower, firmer damping. Over time the oil wears out, picks up metal from the bushes and water past the seals, and gets thinner. The fork then bounces and dives more. The amount of oil also matters: too little and the fork bottoms; too much and it feels hard and can blow the seals.

**Site buying checks:** Use the grade and amount in your manual for that exact fork. Fork oils are sold by weight number (for example 10W), but makers do not grade them the same way, so one brand's 10W can differ from another's. Some manuals give a grade code that is not a W number (K-Light 125: "46#"). Do not assume it equals a W grade; ask the dealer or oil maker for a matching product. Do not use engine oil or gear oil instead of fork oil. Measure the exact quantity per leg with a measuring cylinder, or set the oil level if your manual uses level instead of volume.

**Linked site repairs:** [Replace fork oil and seals Workshop job · 15 min assessment; service time set by the workshop](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/fork-oil-seals/); [Inspect the front forks Rider job · 10 min](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/fork-inspect/); [Clean fork seals Home workshop · 15 to 30 min](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/fork-seal-clean/)

#### Fork seals

**Part ID:** `fork_seals` · [Part guide](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/parts/fork_seals/) · [Existing image reference](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/assets/illustrations/chassis/F18.png) · [Existing shop destination](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/parts/part/fork-seals/)

**Site explanation:** The oil seal has thin lips that wipe the inner tube and keep fork oil inside as the fork moves. The dust seal stops grit and water reaching the oil seal. Dirt, dried insects, rust pits or a scratch on the tube cut the lips, and old rubber goes hard. Once the seal leaks, oil runs down the slider and can reach the brake.

**Site buying checks:** Seal size code: inner diameter × outer diameter × height in mm, for example 37×50×11. The inner diameter equals the fork tube diameter. Check the seal style (single lip, double lip, with or without spring); match the old one or the part number. Genuine or known-brand seals have clean, even lips. Poor seals leak again within weeks. Buy new fork oil at the same time.

**Linked site repairs:** [Clean fork seals Home workshop · 15 to 30 min](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/fork-seal-clean/); [Replace fork oil and seals Workshop job · 15 min assessment; service time set by the workshop](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/fork-oil-seals/); [Inspect the front forks Rider job · 10 min](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/fork-inspect/)

#### Front forks

**Part ID:** `forks` · [Part guide](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/parts/forks/) · [Existing image reference](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/assets/renders/forks.webp) · [Existing shop destination](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/parts/)

**Site explanation:** The spring carries the weight of bike and rider and soaks up bumps. The oil, forced through small holes in the damper rod, slows the movement so the bike does not bounce. A rebound spring stops the fork hitting the top. Seals at the top of the slider keep oil in and dirt out. Bushes let the tubes slide smoothly. Wear comes from dirt on the tubes, old oil, rust pits and crash damage.

**Site buying checks:** Fork seals (sized by inner tube diameter), Fork oil , springs, bushes, dust seals. Inner tubes: match diameter, length and model. Fork springs: match free length and rate. Some bikes use upside-down or cartridge forks with different parts; check the manual.

#### Frame

**Part ID:** `frame` · [Part guide](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/parts/frame/) · [Existing image reference](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/assets/renders/frame.webp) · [Existing shop destination](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/parts/)

**Site explanation:** The frame holds every part in the right place so the wheels stay in line and the bike steers straight. It also carries the engine as part of the structure on many bikes. Crashes, overloading and rough roads can bend it or crack welds and brackets. A bent frame makes the bike pull or weave even when everything else is correct.

**Site buying checks:** People usually buy bolts, Engine mounting bolts , Steering head bearings , Swingarm and bushes , brackets and rubber mounts rather than a frame. A complete frame must match make, model and year, and legally match the vehicle documents.

#### Handlebar and grips

**Part ID:** `handlebar` · [Part guide](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/parts/handlebar/) · [Existing image reference](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/assets/renders/handlebar.webp) · [Existing shop destination](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/parts/)

**Site explanation:** The bar turns the forks. The grips give you a firm hold; the right grip is the throttle and must turn freely and snap back. Falls bend bars and tear grips; loose clamps let the bar rotate in its mounts, which is dangerous.

**Site buying checks:** Bar diameter (22 mm, also called 7/8 inch, is common), width, rise and bend shape. Check that cables and hoses still reach at full lock. Some bars have holes or dowels for switch housings; match those. Grips: right grip inner diameter fits the throttle tube, left fits the bar. Many are sold as a pair.

#### Brake and clutch levers

**Part ID:** `levers` · [Part guide](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/parts/levers/) · [Existing image reference](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/assets/renders/handlebar.webp) · [Existing shop destination](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/parts/part/levers/)

**Site explanation:** The lever multiplies your hand force and pulls a cable or pushes a master cylinder piston. The pivot bolt must be greased so the lever moves smoothly and comes back fully. The brake lever also works the brake light switch. Levers are the first thing to break in a fall; a broken brake lever stub can still be dangerous to use.

**Site buying checks:** Make, model, year, and left or right. The pivot hole, the nub that pushes the master cylinder piston or holds the cable end, and the brake light switch tab must match. Adjustable aftermarket levers must be for your exact master cylinder. Avoid brittle cast levers with rough edges or bubbles in the metal.

#### Rear shock absorbers

**Part ID:** `rear_shock` · [Part guide](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/parts/rear_shock/) · [Existing image reference](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/assets/renders/rear_shock_twin.webp) · [Existing shop destination](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/parts/part/rear-shock/)

**Site explanation:** The spring holds the bike up and soaks up bumps. The damper slows the spring down so the bike does not keep bouncing. Many shocks have a preload adjuster (a stepped collar) to set the spring for a passenger or load. Over time the damper oil leaks or wears out and the spring sags.

**Site buying checks:** Make, model and year. Eye-to-eye length (centre of top mount to centre of bottom mount), mount type (eye or stud) and eye bore size. Spring rate should suit the bike and load. A longer shock raises the seat and changes steering. Check the mounting rubbers or bushes are included. Very cheap shocks often have little damping. Check reviews and the maker's name.

#### Speedometer cable

**Part ID:** `speedo_cable` · [Part guide](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/parts/speedo_cable/) · [Existing image reference](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/assets/renders/instruments_analogue.webp) · [Existing shop destination](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/parts/)

**Site explanation:** A drive gear in the wheel hub turns an inner cable, which spins a magnet in the speedometer. The faster it spins, the higher the needle reads, and it also turns the odometer. The inner cable wears, dries out and breaks, especially if the cable is bent tightly. The hub drive housing must be fitted with its tangs in the hub slots, or the gear is crushed.

**Site buying checks:** Make, model and year. Length, end type (screw nut or clip) at both ends and the square or slotted inner tip. Disc and drum brake versions of one model can use different cables and drive housings. Electronic speedometers do not use a cable; buy the sensor instead.

#### Steering head bearings

**Part ID:** `steering_bearings` · [Part guide](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/parts/steering_bearings/) · [Existing image reference](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/assets/illustrations/chassis/F17.png) · [Existing shop destination](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/parts/)

**Site explanation:** The bearings let the forks and bars turn smoothly from lock to lock while holding the front end tight to the frame. An adjusting nut sets how tight they are. Too loose, the front end clunks and can wobble. Too tight, the steering feels heavy and the bike weaves. Water and old grease wear dents into the races, which you feel as a notch in the centre.

**Site buying checks:** Make, model and year. Check the type: loose balls (count and size), caged balls, or tapered rollers. The ball count and size must match your bike exactly; check the manual or the old parts. Taper roller kits are a common upgrade, but buy one made for your model. Dust seals usually come in the kit. Buy known brands; soft cheap races dent quickly.

#### Swingarm and bushes

**Part ID:** `swingarm` · [Part guide](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/parts/swingarm/) · [Existing image reference](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/assets/renders/swingarm.webp) · [Existing shop destination](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/parts/)

**Site explanation:** The swingarm lets the rear wheel move up and down while keeping it in line with the front. The pivot shaft and bushes must allow smooth up and down movement with no side play. Water and old grease wear the bushes. Worn bushes let the rear wheel steer slightly, which makes the bike wander and wears the chain unevenly. Many scooters use a swinging engine instead of a separate swingarm.

**Site buying checks:** Make, model and year. Bush or bearing type and size, pivot shaft diameter and length, and thread. Buy the bush or bearing set with its collars and seals as a kit. Use waterproof grease on the pivot.

#### Throttle cable

**Part ID:** `throttle_cable` · [Part guide](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/parts/throttle_cable/) · [Existing image reference](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/assets/illustrations/controls/F05.png) · [Existing shop destination](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/parts/part/throttle-cable/)

**Site explanation:** Turning the grip pulls the cable and opens the throttle. A spring at the carburettor or throttle body pulls it shut when you let go. A little slack at the grip (free play) makes sure the throttle closes fully at idle and when you turn the bars. A dry, kinked or frayed cable can stick open, which is very dangerous.

**Site buying checks:** Make, model and year. Length, end fittings, adjuster position and whether it is a single or a pull and return pair. Carburettor and fuel-injected versions of the same model often use different cables. Compare with the old cable before fitting. Cheap cables with rough inner wire stick in the outer.

### Cooling

#### Coolant

**Part ID:** `coolant` · [Part guide](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/parts/coolant/) · [Existing image reference](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/assets/renders/engine_2t.webp) · [Existing shop destination](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/parts/)

**Site explanation:** Coolant carries heat from the hot cylinder and head to the radiator . The antifreeze raises its boiling point, lowers its freezing point, and its inhibitors protect aluminium and the water pump seal from corrosion. Inhibitors get used up with time, so old coolant corrodes the engine from inside even when the level is right.

**Site buying checks:** Use the coolant type your bike's manual names. Honda, for example, asks for ethylene glycol coolant with inhibitors for aluminium engines and warns that silicate inhibitors can wear water pump seals and block radiator passages. Mix with distilled or low-mineral water, not tap water, in the ratio the manual gives, or buy premixed coolant. Do not mix different coolant types or colours; flush the old one out first. Fake or poor coolant may be dyed water. Buy sealed containers from a known brand.

#### Radiator fan

**Part ID:** `cooling_fan` · [Part guide](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/parts/cooling_fan/) · [Existing image reference](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/assets/renders/engine_2t.webp) · [Existing shop destination](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/parts/)

**Site explanation:** When the bike is moving, air flows through the radiator by itself. In slow traffic or at idle there is not enough airflow, so the fan pulls air through. It switches on at a set temperature and off again once the engine cools. Fan motors wear out, blades crack, and the switch, relay, fuse or wiring can fail. Water and mud reach the motor and plug.

**Site buying checks:** Match make, model and year: blade size, mounting points, rotation direction and plug. Fan switches are rated for a switching temperature and thread; match the number on the old switch. Check the fuse rating for the fan circuit in your manual; never fit a larger fuse.

#### Radiator

**Part ID:** `radiator` · [Part guide](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/parts/radiator/) · [Existing image reference](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/assets/renders/engine_2t.webp) · [Existing shop destination](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/parts/)

**Site explanation:** Hot coolant from the engine flows through the thin tubes, and air passing through the fins takes the heat away. The cap holds the system under pressure so the coolant boils at a higher temperature, and lets extra coolant flow to the expansion tank as it heats. Fins get bent by stones and blocked by mud and insects. Old coolant corrodes the inside and silt blocks the tubes.

**Site buying checks:** Match make, model and year: size, hose positions, fan mounts and filler type. Match the cap pressure rating stamped on the old cap. A wrong cap can boil the coolant or burst hoses. Cheap copies may have fewer fins or thinner tubes and cool less.

#### Thermostat

**Part ID:** `thermostat` · [Part guide](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/parts/thermostat/) · [Existing image reference](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/assets/renders/engine_2t.webp) · [Existing shop destination](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/parts/)

**Site explanation:** When the engine is cold, the thermostat stays closed so coolant circulates only inside the engine and it warms up quickly. As the coolant heats, the wax melts and expands, pushing the valve open so coolant flows to the radiator. A thermostat stuck shut makes the engine overheat fast. One stuck open makes the engine slow to warm, which raises fuel use and wear.

**Site buying checks:** Match the part number or the opening temperature, size and shape. A thermostat with the wrong opening temperature changes how hot the engine runs. Check the small bleed hole or jiggle valve is in the same place as on the old one. Never run without a thermostat to "cure" overheating; find the real cause.

#### Water pump

**Part ID:** `water_pump` · [Part guide](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/parts/water_pump/) · [Existing image reference](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/assets/renders/engine_2t.webp) · [Existing shop destination](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/parts/)

**Site explanation:** The impeller spins and pushes coolant through the engine and radiator . The seal keeps coolant out of the engine oil on one side and in the pump on the other. If the seal wears, coolant drips from the weep hole or gets into the oil. Hard deposits from tap water or wrong coolant wear the seal faster; a broken impeller stops flow.

**Site buying checks:** Match make, model and year, or the engine code. Impeller size and shaft drive differ. Buy the housing gasket and O-rings with it. Use the right coolant afterwards; Honda warns that silicate coolant can wear water pump seals.

### Exhaust

#### Exhaust and silencer

**Part ID:** `exhaust` · [Part guide](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/parts/exhaust/) · [Existing image reference](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/assets/renders/exhaust_4t.webp) · [Existing shop destination](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/parts/)

**Site explanation:** The exhaust lets the engine breathe out, cuts noise, and on newer bikes cleans the gas: the catalytic converter burns leftover fuel and carbon monoxide. The pipe and silencer rust from the inside, mounts crack from vibration, and carbon builds up, especially on two-strokes and engines that burn oil. A melted or blocked catalyst chokes the engine.

**Site buying checks:** Match make, model and year. A wrong pipe changes power and fuel use, and on injected bikes can trip the warning light. On bikes sold with a catalyst, buy a part with one. The K-Light silencer carries approval marks; many countries require a marked, legal silencer. Loud "free-flow" silencers and removed baffles are often illegal and can make the engine run lean and hot.

#### Exhaust gasket

**Part ID:** `exhaust_gasket` · [Part guide](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/parts/exhaust_gasket/) · [Existing image reference](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/assets/renders/exhaust_4t.webp) · [Existing shop destination](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/parts/)

**Site explanation:** The gasket seals the hot, pulsing gas where the pipe meets the head. It crushes a little when the flange is tightened, filling small gaps. Heat cycles flatten and burn it. A leak lets air into the pipe, which upsets the oxygen sensor, and lets hot gas burn the port face.

**Site buying checks:** Match the engine code or the inside and outside diameter and thickness of the old ring. Many commuter singles share sizes, but check. Match the type: plain crush ring, ring with a lip, or graphite sandwich. Cheap rings may be too hard to crush and seal. Buy from a dealer or a known gasket maker.

**Linked site repairs:** [Find and fix an exhaust leak Home workshop · 30 to 60 min](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/exhaust-leak-check/); [Check exhaust mounts and heat shields Rider job · 15 to 30 min](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/exhaust-mount-check/); [Check the oxygen sensor Workshop job · 10 min for home checks; 30 to 60 min at a workshop](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/o2-sensor-check/); [Decarbonise a two-stroke exhaust and port Workshop job · 2 to 4 h](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/two-stroke-decoke/)

**Linked site symptoms:** [Ticking or puffing from an exhaust leak Ride with care](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/problems/exhaust-leak/); [Popping or banging from the exhaust when slowing down Ride with care](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/problems/exhaust-popping/); [Uses more fuel than normal OK to ride](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/problems/high-fuel-use/); [Exhaust blocked or choked with carbon (two-stroke) Ride with care](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/problems/exhaust-blocked/); [Exhaust has become much louder Ride with care](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/problems/exhaust-loud/); [Oil dripping from the exhaust (two-stroke) Ride with care](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/problems/oily-exhaust/); [Engine runs hot and lean, pops and pinks Ride with care](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/problems/runs-lean/); [Ticking noise from the top of the engine Ride with care](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/problems/tappet-tick/)

## Sources, attribution and research gaps

### Source register

- [Moto Zero part index](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/parts/): current part taxonomy, asset paths and shop links.
- [Moto Zero repair index](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/repairs/): existing repair IDs and titles.
- [Moto Zero symptom index](https://motobike-five.vercel.app/repair/problems/): existing symptom IDs and titles.
- [VehiclesDB](https://vehiclesdb.com), [repository](https://github.com/vehiclesdb/vehiclesdb), [schema](https://github.com/vehiclesdb/vehiclesdb/blob/main/SCHEMA.md), [sources](https://github.com/vehiclesdb/vehiclesdb/blob/main/SOURCES.md), [attribution](https://github.com/vehiclesdb/vehiclesdb/blob/main/ATTRIBUTION.md): identity and covered-country observations. This reference adapts a subset, assigns editorial categories and adds repair-topic mappings. No upstream endorsement is implied.
- [Honda manuals/parts catalogues](https://www.hondamotopub.com/HMJ), [Yamaha parts finder](https://yamaha-motor.com/parts/motorcycle), [Bajaj Kenya owner manuals](https://www.bajajauto.com/en-ke/owners-zone), [TVS Kenya service](https://www.tvsmotor.com/en/ke/service), [Haojue service manuals](https://www.haojuemotor.com/motorcycles-service-manual/), [NIU downloads](https://global.niu.com/downloads): next-stage verification sources. Their presence here does not mean every manual was downloaded or every fitment checked.
- [API Ninjas](https://api-ninjas.com/api/motorcycles) and [Data & APIs](https://dataandapis.com/apis/motorcycles): evaluated as potential catalogue-enrichment providers, not used as purchased or authenticated data sources. No subscription was created.

### Remaining work before treating this as a production fitment database

1. Resolve every candidate identity and review official-page name matches. Record generation, market and year for all 500.
2. Add exact specifications from the appropriate manufacturer manual; keep public product specifications separate from workshop tolerances.
3. Review every proposed model-to-part relationship. The links are useful for content planning now, but do not establish hardware on every version.
4. Obtain OEM numbers, supersessions and verified configuration ranges. No SKU-fitment claims were established in this edition.
5. Review model-specific repair methods, service intervals, torque values and limits. The existing site’s example specifications must not be generalised.
6. Add photo assets only after identity and rights checks. No photo assets have been attached in this edition.
7. Add comparable model sales/registration observations by country and period; do not turn editorial ordering into a bestseller list.
8. Expand underrepresented Chinese, Latin American and African local brands and EV manufacturers, using country evidence and demand. This 500-model selection is a starting coverage budget, not exhaustive global coverage.

### Candidates requiring an individual identity source

No completely unsourced candidate identities remain. Official-catalogue and search-evidence matches still require variant review.
